faq.q: Can you charter a yacht in Marbella in November?
faq.a: Yes. November is part of the low season, but most boats in our fleet operate year-round. We depart from Puerto Banús daily, weather permitting. The sea is calm, and you’ll enjoy more privacy and often lower rates than summer.

faq.q: What is the sea temperature in Marbella in November?
faq.a: The Mediterranean off Marbella averages 18°C in November. That’s too cool for casual swimming without a wetsuit, but fine for paddling or jet skiing. If you want to swim, a short-sleeve wetsuit (3/2mm) keeps you comfortable.

faq.q: What should I wear for a November yacht charter in Marbella?
faq.a: Layers. A long-sleeve top + light jacket or fleece works for the morning breeze. By midday (18-20°C), you may shed layers. Closed-toe non-slip shoes are smart. Sunglasses and sunscreen are still essential – UV is strong even in autumn.

faq.q: How many hours of daylight do you get in November?
faq.a: Sunrise is around 07:45 and sunset about 18:00, giving you roughly 10 hours of daylight. For a half-day charter (4-5 hours), aim for a 10:00 or 11:00 departure to enjoy the best light. Full-day charters (8 hours) work well if you start by 09:30.

faq.q: Do you offer any boats with heating or enclosed cabins?
faq.a: All our boats have enclosed saloons with heating and air conditioning. Flybridge models like the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) have a heated lower helm station. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) also offers a spacious, climate-controlled interior.

faq.q: What happens if bad weather is forecast on my charter day?
faq.a: Your safety is our priority. If forecasts show unsafe conditions (e.g. >25 knot winds or heavy rain), we’ll contact you to reschedule or cancel at no charge. November storms are rare and short-lived – usually passing within a few hours.

faq.q: Are November charters cheaper than summer?

data.body_html:
Thinking about a Marbella yacht charter in November? You might be wondering if the weather holds up. The short answer: yes. November on the Costa del Sol offers mild air (15-20°C), calm seas, and fewer crowds – a surprisingly pleasant window for a relaxed cruise. This guide covers everything you need to know: sea temperature, wind, daylight, rain, and which boats suit the season.

November Weather Overview for Marbella

November is late autumn, but Marbella’s microclimate keeps it milder than inland Spain. Average highs reach 20°C, lows drop to 13°C. The sea temperature sits around 18°C – cool but not freezing. You’ll get roughly 10 hours of daylight, with sunset near 18:00. Rain is possible (5-7 wet days on average), but showers are usually brief and pass quickly. The Sierra Blanca mountains shield the coast from strong winds, so the sea stays flat for most of the month.

Sea Temperature & Swimming Conditions

The Mediterranean off Marbella averages 18°C in November. That’s a few degrees cooler than September (23°C) and October (21°C). For swimming, most people find it too chilly without a wetsuit. A 3/2mm short-sleeve wetsuit makes it comfortable. If you’re booking a Marbella yacht charter primarily for water sports, consider a boat that includes a jet ski – like the Mangusta 80 (€4,719 for 4 hours, jet ski included free) – because the adrenaline keeps you warm.

Wind & Sea State

November is one of the calmest months for wind along the Costa del Sol. Average wind speeds are 5-15 knots, often lighter in the morning. The famous Levante (easterly) wind is rare in autumn. Swell heights typically stay below 0.5-1 metre. That means smooth cruising for all our boats, from the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) up to the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax). If you’re prone to seasickness, November is a safe bet.

Daylight Hours & Best Charter Times

Sunrise: ~07:45. Sunset: ~18:00. That’s about 10 hours of usable daylight – enough for a half-day (4-5 hours) or full-day (8 hours) charter. For a half-day, a 10:00 or 11:00 start gives you the warmest part of the day. Full-day charters depart around 09:30 and return by 17:30, catching the golden hour. Popular November itineraries include a cruise from Puerto Banús to Cala del Faro (30 min) or a longer run to Estepona (45 min) for lunch ashore.

Rain & Cloud Cover

November averages 5-7 rainy days, but total precipitation is only about 60-80mm. Showers are typically short (15-30 minutes) and often happen overnight or early morning. Cloud cover varies: some days are bright with scattered clouds, others are completely clear. If you’re flexible, you can usually dodge rain by shifting your departure by an hour. All our boats have enclosed saloons with heating, so even a passing shower won’t ruin the trip.

Best Boats for November Charters

For cooler weather, boats with covered flybridges or spacious indoor saloons are ideal. Our top picks:

  • Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) – heated lower helm, enclosed flybridge, stable ride.
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) – huge saloon, jet ski included, departs Puerto Banús.
  • Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) – luxury interior, full climate control, perfect for entertaining.
  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) – affordable option with a cosy cabin, €749/2h.

All our charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, soft drinks, beer, wine, cava, light snacks, and 21% IVA. You can book online or message us on WhatsApp for custom quotes.

What to Pack for a November Yacht Charter

Layers are your friend. Start with a long-sleeve shirt or light sweater, add a fleece or windbreaker, and bring a waterproof shell just in case. Non-slip deck shoes (or trainers with good grip) are essential. Sunglasses and sunscreen are still necessary – UV index is moderate but reflection off the water adds exposure. A hat and a small towel are handy. If you plan to use the jet ski, a wetsuit is recommended (we can advise on local rental shops).
